The earlier grading/reference uncertainty is resolved for the ordinary A∞ intrinsic-formality criterion actually asserted. [Kadeishvili, §2 and Corollary 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0210331) uses cochains of arity n and internal degree 2−n, and concludes that every minimal higher structure with the given binary product is equivalent to the trivial higher structure. [Keller §§3.1, 3.3 and 3.5](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bernhard.keller/publ/ioan.pdf) explicitly separates ordinary A∞ algebras from the subsequent strict-unital theory.

In the [actual vanishing predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality/Criterion.lean#L80), a suspended degree-q cochain of arity n has original internal degree q+1−n. Thus its degree-one arity-n cocycle has degree 2−n, as does the degree-zero arity-(n−1) primitive. The [differential](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Hochschild/Basic.lean#L73) is the graded bracket with the binary multiplication; the [proved arity identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Obstruction.lean#L205) confirms that it raises arity by one. Positive tensor lengths omit arity zero, which does not affect the cocycles and boundaries used for n≥3. This is not normalized cohomology obtained by quotienting out a unit.

The [conclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality.lean#L80) quantifies over all A∞ algebras with the prescribed cohomology algebra and concludes ordinary formality; it does not promise a unit-preserving equivalence. Therefore the theorem is a correctly scoped ordinary criterion, while the roadmap's additional strict-unital normalization remains an enhancement, not a hidden hypothesis or claimed conclusion here. The [roadmap acceptance table](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity/README.md#L677) explicitly assigns the exterior/quiver transfer examples to Layer 3, not this Layer 8 criterion; my previous review overextended those checks. No separate intrinsic-formality Check is prescribed there. The actual [degree-zero intrinsic-formality theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/IntrinsicFormality.lean#L182) supplies a nonvacuous boundary calibration. The previous reference gap is resolved by [Jørgensen's own 1979 paper, Proposition 1 and its discussion on pp.90–91](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/6BDE9DE2806F4A5B5744938995A7EE85/S0008414X0001141Xa.pdf/div-class-title-comments-on-a-discreteness-condition-for-subgroups-of-sl-2-c-div.pdf): the trace inequality holds for discrete non-elementary pairs, with exceptional elementary pairs preserving the first element's fixed-point set. Its `tr(A²)−2` equals `(tr A)²−4` for determinant-one matrices. For real elliptic A, a real orientation-preserving Möbius map preserving its conjugate fixed-point pair must fix the upper-half-plane point; the stabilizer is abelian, giving precisely the project's projective-commutation exception. Alternatively the only noncyclic elementary Fuchsian case has elliptic half-turns, whose trace is zero and first absolute-value term is already 4. Thus no non-elementarity assumption was accidentally dropped.

The [pinned theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/Jorgensen.lean#L418) uses genuine SL₂(ℝ) lifts in a discrete PSL₂(ℝ) subgroup, the strict elliptic condition, and the standard commutator order. Both sides and the exception are unchanged by lift signs; ±I fail ellipticity. The [commutator-displacement formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Displacement.lean#L171) checks the constants independently of the inequality: its left side becomes `(4−tr²A)(1+cosh d)/2`. The [geometric form](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/Jorgensen.lean#L404) agrees by the half-angle identity. These source witnesses are proved without sorry.

Correctly stated as the vector-field Fréchet subdifferential. The earlier all-optimal-versus-infimum concern is resolved by a comparison with [AGS2005, Proposition8.5.4 and (10.3.13)](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~sayan/ambrosio.pdf). Here is the additional argument, rather than an assumed equivalence. Project ξ orthogonally onto the L²-closure of smooth cylindrical gradients. The discarded divergence-free component pairs to zero with every optimal displacement by Proposition8.5.4. For a smooth cylindrical f, Taylor's formula and equal marginals bound the difference of its pairings along two optimal plans by `||D²f||∞ W₂²`. Approximating the tangent projection by ∇f changes each pairing by at most `||ξ_tan−∇f||₂ W₂`. Consequently the difference is uniformly `o(W₂)`. Taking an infimum or requiring every optimal plan therefore gives the same first-order inequality for vector fields, even at singular laws. This does not identify the definition with the distinct extended plan or all-coupling strong notions.

The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Subdifferential.lean#L106) uses the actual P₂ carrier and L² classes, excludes both infinite energies at μ, and uses the W₂ neighborhood with the correct negative ε-error. Marginal preservation and Cauchy–Schwarz give representative independence and integrability. Optimal plans exist under the complete separable hypotheses, so the quantifier is not vacuous; at ν=μ its displacement vanishes.

The definition uses `LinearMap.toMatrix` with the indecomposable-projective basis as domain and the simple-class basis as codomain. [The entry theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/CartanMatrix.lean#L147) proves Cᵢⱼ=[Pⱼ:Sᵢ], so the row/column orientation is explicit. Its coefficients are integers obtained from genuine natural composition multiplicities. Exhaustivity and pairwise nonisomorphism are hypotheses for both bases; arbitrary duplicate lists cannot silently produce a matrix of the intended map.

The chosen families share an indexing type but need not be matched by projective-cover maps. This is sufficient for the stated matrix in two selected bases; independently reordering them reorders rows and columns. It does not by itself identify the separately defined coordinate pairing with raw Hom dimension. The latter requires the projective-cover matching and the division-algebra correction described by the roadmap. The target makes no unconditional unimodularity claim; the [dual-number test](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/DualNumbers.lean#L139) computes this exact matrix as [2], as required.
